tweets.author: @darioamodei
tweets.text: Today I'm publishing a new essay, Policy on the AI Exponential. AI is progressing extremely fast—much faster than the policy process was built to handle. The essay lays out where I think the technology is now, and the action needed to close the gap:

tweets.author: @tenobrus
tweets.text: the specificity of this proposal is so insanely head and shoulders above openai's recent article as to make it laughable.  i'm basically on board with everything proposed, and think this is extremely worth reading.  unfortunately i worry anthropic does not in fact have the regulatory influence to actually make most of these things happen [...]

tweets.author: @jconorgrogan
tweets.text: TLDR: 1.  Declare AI too dangerous for ordinary competition so you propose a regulatory regime where only the largest incumbents can survive 2.  Warn about labor displacement while selling the product to executives as a labor-displacement tool 3.  Warn about state overreach while asking the state to license and gatekeep frontier models 4.  Warn about corporate power while sketching a corporate-state cartel over compute, release, security, export controls, and deployment

tweets.text: Fable seems totally unusable currently due to the over zealous rejection classifier, even for non related to cyber security. Can't see why anyone would use this over Opus.

tweets.text: @tautologer it is the first publicly available model that i am explicitly not allowed to use for my work, because anthropic holds the view that the work i do to facilitate open model research is harmful. capability and alignment research are coupled. anthropic wants to be the only lab.

tweets.text: What's crazy to me is that Fable is blocked from life sciences broadly, nerfed even if you get passed the classifiers and filter level blocks. The whole point of AGI/ASI is to cure all diseases. Everything else is just nice to haves. But Anthropic wants to close off that path.

top news.title: Google introduces DiffusionGemma, an experimental 26B-parameter open model that uses text diffusion for faster text generation compared to autoregressive models

tweets.author: @_philschmid
tweets.text: Gemma goes diffusion! DiffusionGemma with up to 1000+ tokens per second! 🌬️ - Built on Gemma 4 as a 26B MoE model. - 3.8B parameters during inference. - Generates text in 256-token blocks in parallel. - Fits within 18 GB VRAM limits when quantized. - Apache 2.0 [video]

tweets.author: @omarsar0
tweets.text: This is awesome! I am spending a lot of time on diffusion LLMs these days, so this is perfect timing. I feel like there are so many underexplored research questions around text diffusion. Weight available in HF. [image]

tweets.author: @vllm_project
tweets.text: Congrats to @GoogleDeepMind on DiffusionGemma 🎉 A 26B diffusion language model on the Gemma4 backbone, and the first dLLM natively supported in vLLM.  It denoises 256-token blocks in parallel instead of generating one token at a time: 1200+ output tok/s at batch size 1 on a single H200 (FP8).  Built on model runner v2's ModelState plus the existing speculative decoding path, with minimal scheduler or runner changes.  FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints are on the @RedHat_AI hub.  Thanks to the @GoogleDeepMind , @RedHat_AI , and @NVIDIAAI teams!
